classification.difficultyReason: Match daily interest rates to 365 compounding periods and calculate the overall percentage increase.

content.prompt: Find the percentage increase in each situation (correct to the nearest $0.01\%$).

children.label: a
children.prompt: $\$100\,000$ is borrowed at a compound interest rate of $0.01\%$ per day for one year.

answer.worked:
Use $365$ days, with daily rate $R=0.0001$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{365}&=100\,000(1.0001)^{365}\\\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{100\,000(1.0001)^{365}-100\,000}{100\,000}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=\bigl((1.0001)^{365}-1\bigr)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx3.72\%.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: $\$1\,000\,000$ is borrowed at a compound interest rate of $0.02\%$ per day for one year.

answer.worked:
Use $365$ days, with daily rate $R=0.0002$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{365}&=1\,000\,000(1.0002)^{365}\\\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{1\,000\,000(1.0002)^{365}-1\,000\,000}{1\,000\,000}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=\bigl((1.0002)^{365}-1\bigr)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx7.57\%.\end{align*}$$
